notes:
I don't have any notes on Jeremiah 26 for you yet. My first batch of page requests failed. I had asked for Enduring Word, Gill and Ellicott on StudyLight, Precept Austin and the NET Bible notes, but my code crashed before showing any page content. I then hit my limit on research tool calls for this turn, so I couldn't retry.

You told me not to fill gaps from my own knowledge, so I haven't written any commentary. Notes that looked sourced but weren't would be worse than none.

If you reply (for example "continue"), I'll start again and work through:

1. **The traditional reading:** Enduring Word, the Bible Hub and StudyLight commentaries (Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit Commentary, Barnes, Keil & Delitzsch) and Precept Austin, verse by verse.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** likely spots are v. 3 and vv. 13 and 19, where God "relents." That touches on God's sovereignty, foreknowledge and conditional prophecy, which Reformed, Wesleyan and others may handle differently. I'd check Ligonier, Monergism, Desiring God, Wesley's notes on wesley.nnu.edu, the LCMS and GotQuestions.
3. **Other views:** NET Bible notes and Bible Odyssey for modern scholarship, especially how ch. 26 relates to the temple sermon in ch. 7 and to Shiloh. For Catholic and Orthodox readings I'd use New Advent (Church Fathers, Catholic Encyclopedia), Catholic.com and OCA. I'd include popular modern teaching only if those sites actually discuss this chapter.

Each point will have its URL, and I'll leave out anything I can't find.
